attribution.note: Zitron's own words in his own post, stated firmly ("I must be clear").

semantics.note: "Cannot slow down without creating" is a firm conditional: if AI slows down, a serious tech financial crisis follows. The antecedent is kept and there is no hedge. No deadline.

contract.note: Reading "slowdown" as material cuts to lab compute demand comes from his own mechanism ("slow their roll", demand contraction, revenue restatements). That is an ordinary, fair reading. No deadline, so scoring waits on the antecedent.

evidence.note: Anthropic's S-1 shows about $417B in compute obligations plus more ordered. This shows the antecedent (a demand contraction) had not occurred. It is not evidence of the consequent.
Secondary report that Anthropic's commitments rose to $517B while its CEO urged a slowdown. Bears on the antecedent being unmet, not on the outcome.
OpenAI's training pauses were safety holds, not cuts to compute commitments. The antecedent is not met.
Neocloud stocks fell over 30% in October amid credit risk, but this is not tied to any lab demand contraction. Cannot score the conditional.

reviews.rationale: Conditional forecast with no deadline. By 2026-10-28 the evidence shows lab compute commitments growing, not contracting, and the OpenAI pauses were safety holds. The antecedent is not met, so the claim cannot be scored. The neocloud stress is not linked to a slowdown. A slowdown could still occur later.
